title: Hungry for the new
paragraphs: What did you eat for lunch today? Did you choose this dish because it was healthy, cheap or because it was just very tasty? Are you a fussy eater or an adventurous gourmet?

I love exploring trends in food. 'Fusion cuisine' is not for everybody. My Italian grandmother would turn her nose up in disgust at the thought of tandoori pizza with mango topping but this marriage of tastes is perfectly fine in the 21st century.

Chef and food writer Ching-He Huang, who presented a series on Chinese Food for the BBC, is a fan of the movement. She says: "Fusion has been happening for centuries, for as long as people have travelled, but with the internet, and global travel, the exchange of ideas makes the process much faster."

Wolfgang Puck is seen by many as one of the chefs who made 'fusion' elegant. He cut his teeth in his native Vienna and made a name for himself when he opened his own restaurant in Los Angeles in the 1970s. This European delved into Asian cuisine and became one of the first in a long line of celebrity chefs.

He said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal that initially he got negative responses from traditional American-Chinese restaurant owners but he is not bitter. "I believe authenticity is about evolution, not repeating your grandmother's recipe," he explains. "Cooking is like painting or writing a song. Just as there are only so many notes or colours, there are only so many flavours – it's how you combine them that sets you apart."

My granny's preference would be the Slow Food Movement. Founded by her countryman Carlo Petrini in the 1980s and still going strong, it seeks to preserve regional cuisine and the use of ingredients that are grown locally. Petrini wants to see farmers connected more directly with consumers.

All these trends give us food for thought. We might be wasting an exciting opportunity to wake up our taste buds when we scoff a sandwich at our desks. Tomorrow, why not find an exotic restaurant and enjoy a feast? You dress trendy so eat trendy!

vocabulary.entry: fussy eater /ˈfʌsi ˈiːtə(r)/ 挑食的人（短语）
vocabulary.example: My little brother is a very fussy eater.
vocabulary.translation: 我的弟弟吃饭非常挑食。

vocabulary.entry: adventurous /ədˈventʃərəs/ adj. 乐于尝试的；猎奇的
vocabulary.example: She is adventurous and loves strange foreign food.
vocabulary.translation: 她勇于尝试，喜欢小众异国美食。

vocabulary.entry: gourmet /ˈɡɔːmeɪ/ n. 美食家；美食爱好者
vocabulary.example: A true gourmet can tell different flavours easily.
vocabulary.translation: 真正的美食家能轻松分辨各类风味。

vocabulary.entry: fusion cuisine /ˈfjuːʒn kwɪˈziːn/ 融合料理；混搭美食（短语）
vocabulary.example: This restaurant is famous for its fusion cuisine.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅以融合特色料理闻名。

vocabulary.entry: turn one's nose up /tɜːn wʌnz nəʊz ʌp/ 嗤之以鼻；瞧不起（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: He turns his nose up at simple home-made food.
vocabulary.translation: 他对家常简餐嗤之以鼻。

vocabulary.entry: topping /ˈtɒpɪŋ/ n. 配料；浇头
vocabulary.example: I added fruit topping on the cake.
vocabulary.translation: 我在蛋糕上加了水果配料。

vocabulary.entry: cut one's teeth /kʌt wʌnz tiːθ/ 初次历练；积累经验（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: The young chef cut his teeth in a small local restaurant.
vocabulary.translation: 这位年轻厨师在本地小餐馆积累了从业经验。

vocabulary.entry: make a name for oneself /meɪk ə neɪm fɔː(r) wʌnˈself/ 成名；崭露头角（短语）
vocabulary.example: She made a name for herself with special cooking skills.
vocabulary.translation: 她凭借独特厨艺一举成名。

vocabulary.entry: delve into /delv ˈɪntuː/ 深入研究；钻研（短语）
vocabulary.example: The chef delves into traditional Eastern cooking.
vocabulary.translation: 这位厨师潜心研究东方传统烹饪。

vocabulary.entry: cuisine /kwɪˈziːn/ n. 菜系；烹饪风格
vocabulary.example: I love authentic Italian cuisine very much.
vocabulary.translation: 我十分正宗的意大利菜系。

vocabulary.entry: celebrity chef /səˈlebrəti ʃef/ 明星厨师；知名主厨（短语）
vocabulary.example: Many celebrity chefs have their own TV shows.
vocabulary.translation: 许多明星厨师都有专属电视节目。

vocabulary.entry: negative response /ˈneɡətɪv rɪˈspɒns/ 负面反馈；反对意见（短语）
vocabulary.example: His new cooking style got a negative response at first.
vocabulary.translation: 他的新式烹饪起初遭到了负面评价。

vocabulary.entry: bitter /ˈbɪtə(r)/ adj. 心怀不满的；愤愤不平的
vocabulary.example: She felt bitter after receiving unfair comments.
vocabulary.translation: 收到不公评价后，她心生不满。

vocabulary.entry: authenticity /ˌɔːθenˈtɪsəti/ n. 正宗；原汁原味
vocabulary.example: The restaurant keeps the authenticity of local food.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅保留了本地美食的原汁原味。

vocabulary.entry: evolution /ˌiːvəˈluːʃn/ n. 演变；革新发展
vocabulary.example: The evolution of cooking brings new tastes.
vocabulary.translation: 烹饪方式的革新催生了全新风味。

vocabulary.entry: set apart /set əˈpɑːt/ 使与众不同；脱颖而出（短语）
vocabulary.example: Creative ideas set great cooks apart.
vocabulary.translation: 创意想法让优秀厨师脱颖而出。

vocabulary.entry: one's cup of tea /wʌnz kʌp ɒv tiː/ 合心意的事物；喜好（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: Simple healthy food is always my cup of tea.
vocabulary.translation: 清淡健康的食物一直合我胃口。

vocabulary.entry: preserve /prɪˈzɜːv/ v. 保护；留存
vocabulary.example: We should preserve traditional local food culture.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应当保护传统地方饮食文化。

vocabulary.entry: ingredient /ɪnˈɡriːdiənt/ n. 食材；原料
vocabulary.example: Fresh ingredients are the key to delicious food.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜食材是美食的关键。

vocabulary.entry: food for thought /fuːd fɔː(r) θɔːt/ 引人深思的事（短语）
vocabulary.example: Different food trends give us much food for thought.
vocabulary.translation: 多样的饮食潮流值得我们深思。

vocabulary.entry: taste bud /teɪst bʌd/ 味蕾（短语）
vocabulary.example: Spicy food can fully excite your taste buds.
vocabulary.translation: 辣味美食能充分唤醒你的味蕾。

vocabulary.entry: scoff /skɒf/ v. 狼吞虎咽地吃；仓促进食
vocabulary.example: People often scoff fast food during busy work.
vocabulary.translation: 人们忙碌工作时常常仓促吃快餐。

vocabulary.entry: exotic /ɪɡˈzɒtɪk/ adj. 异域的；外来特色的
vocabulary.example: We tried some exotic dishes from Southeast Asia.
vocabulary.translation: 我们品尝了一些东南亚异域特色菜肴。

vocabulary.entry: feast /fiːst/ n. 盛宴；丰盛大餐
vocabulary.example: We enjoyed a big feast on the holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在假期享用了一顿丰盛大餐。

vocabulary.entry: trendy /ˈtrendi/ adj. 时髦的；潮流的
vocabulary.example: Trendy healthy diets are popular among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 潮流健康的饮食方式深受年轻人喜爱。

sentences.chinese: 她说：“融合菜已经存在了几个世纪，因为只要人们旅行，它就在发生。但随着互联网和全球旅行的发展，思想的交流使这一过程变得更快。”

sentences.english: Wolfgang Puck is seen by many as one of the chefs who made 'fusion' elegant.
sentences.chinese: 沃尔夫冈·帕克（Wolfgang Puck）被许多人视为是使“融合菜”变得优雅的厨师之一。

sentences.english: He cut his teeth in his native Vienna and made a name for himself when he opened his own restaurant in Los Angeles in the 1970s.
sentences.chinese: 他在家乡维也纳积累了经验，并在20世纪70年代在洛杉矶开设自己的餐厅时一举成名。

sentences.chinese: 这位欧洲厨师深入研究了亚洲美食，并成为众多名厨中的先驱之一。

sentences.english: "I believe authenticity is about evolution, not repeating your grandmother's recipe," he explains.
sentences.chinese: 他解释说：“我相信本真是关于进化，而不是重复你祖母的食谱。

sentences.english: "Cooking is like painting or writing a song.
sentences.chinese: 烹饪就像绘画或写歌。

sentences.english: Just as there are only so many notes or colours, there are only so many flavours – it's how you combine them that sets you apart."
sentences.chinese: 正如音符或颜色有限，味道也是有限的——真正让你脱颖而出的是你如何组合它们。”

sentences.english: My granny's preference would be the Slow Food Movement.
sentences.chinese: 我祖母更喜欢“慢食运动”。

sentences.english: Founded by her countryman Carlo Petrini in the 1980s and still going strong, it seeks to preserve regional cuisine and the use of ingredients that are grown locally.
sentences.chinese: 该运动由她的同胞卡洛·佩特里尼（Carlo Petrini）于20世纪80年代创立，至今仍然蓬勃发展，旨在保护地方美食和使用本地种植的食材。

sentences.english: Petrini wants to see farmers connected more directly with consumers.
sentences.chinese: 佩特里尼希望看到农民与消费者更直接地联系起来。

sentences.chinese: 所有这些趋势都值得我们仔细思考。
